items.title: Russian drones reportedly strike Izmail port facilities and cargo vessel
items.summary: Russian forces reportedly carried out overnight drone strikes on port infrastructure at Izmail used to unload and store military supplies. The same account alleges a dry-cargo vessel carrying dual-use goods toward the port of Pivdennyi was also hit at sea; details of the damage were not provided.

items.title: Russia claims capture of Zalivne amid fighting in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reportedly announced the capture of Zalivne on the Tersyanka–Voskresenka sector of the Zaporizhzhia front. Fighting was also reported near Orikhiv and Novodanylivka, with Russian forces said to be expanding their positions west of Orikhiv.

items.title: Russian drone strikes reportedly target four locomotives in Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Footage circulated of reported Geran drone strikes on railway locomotives, including three in Dnipro and one in Zaporizhzhia. The account identifies four separate targets but does not establish the extent of damage or whether rail operations were disrupted.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 184 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences destroyed 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones between the evening of November 17 and the morning of November 18 over Belgorod and Rostov regions, Krasnodar Krai, Crimea and the Sea of Azov. The ministry did not provide a detailed breakdown of damage or casualties in the cited update.

items.title: Gas carrier reportedly struck by drones off Bulgaria
items.summary: The Liberian-flagged gas carrier GAS HUSKY, reportedly carrying 3,400 tonnes of propane and described as linked to Ukraine's gas fleet, was allegedly hit by four drones roughly 100 kilometres off Bulgaria's coast. Footage circulating online appears to show the vessel burning; the extent of damage and any casualties were not specified.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker says recruitment-centre confrontations have declined
items.summary: Ukrainian parliamentary defence committee member Fedir Venislavskyi said confrontations involving territorial recruitment centres have largely subsided. He added that men aged 50–60 are being mobilized less often, although they remain eligible for conscription.

items.title: Drone attacks reportedly injure eight in Krasnodar Krai and Adygea
items.summary: Regional authorities reportedly said overnight Ukrainian drone attacks injured eight people across Krasnodar Krai and Adygea. Drone debris sparked fires at two enterprises in Krasnodar Krai, while an apartment building in Enem, Adygea, was struck, with four people reportedly injured there.

items.title: Russia reportedly proposes NATO troop limits in wider Ukraine negotiations
items.summary: A reported Russian proposal would bar NATO troop deployments in countries that joined the alliance after 1997 in exchange for reducing Russia's military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus. The account says US representatives have discussed European troop deployments and security arrangements with Russia and Ukraine as part of possible war-ending terms; European leaders reportedly opposed withdrawing NATO forces from Eastern Europe.

items.title: Power outages reported in parts of Kyiv after strikes
items.summary: Several districts of Kyiv reportedly lost electricity following strikes on the Ukrainian capital. The affected districts, number of customers and expected restoration times were not specified in the initial account.

items.title: Ukrainian lawmaker alleges major misuse of Kyiv energy-protection funds
items.summary: Ukrainian parliament member Nagorniak reportedly alleged that up to 700 million hryvnias of an 800-million-hryvnia allocation for protecting energy infrastructure in Kyiv region went to contractors unrelated to building the defenses. The figures and alleged misuse are attributed to his account, rather than established findings of an investigation.

items.title: Finland's president rejects report of Russian demand to leave NATO
items.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb denied a Bild account alleging that Russia had demanded Finland withdraw from NATO during talks in Abu Dhabi. He urged readers not to take the reported proposal seriously, according to comments cited by Finnish newspaper Ilta-Sanomat.

items.title: Crew of stricken gas carrier reportedly rescued off Bulgaria
items.summary: All 19 crew members of the Liberian-flagged GAS HUSKY were reportedly rescued by Bulgarian forces after the vessel caught fire and sank off Bulgaria's coast. Two sailors reportedly sustained minor injuries; the account says the ship had been sailing from Alexandria toward Romania's Midia port when it was struck by an unidentified weapon.

items.title: Russia says it hit Ukrainian drone facilities and downed 310 drones
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck Ukrainian drone manufacturing and storage sites over the past day and that air defenses shot down 310 fixed-wing Ukrainian drones. The ministry also estimated Ukrainian personnel losses at around 1,165, a battlefield figure that remains a Russian military assertion.

items.title: US and European representatives set for Berlin talks on Ukraine security
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are reportedly due to meet Ukrainian and European representatives in Berlin on November 19 to discuss security guarantees and Ukraine's post-war economic recovery. The planned meeting comes amid differences over ceasefire terms and Europe's role in negotiations.

items.title: Kremlin says Putin and Xi discussed Ukraine settlement in Shenzhen
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping discussed efforts to settle the war in Ukraine during their talks in Shenzhen. Putin also mentioned his contacts with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow; no new agreement was announced.

items.title: Russian ambassador disputes Moldova's protest over drone incursions
items.summary: Russia's ambassador called Moldova's diplomatic protest over recent drone incursions unfounded, suggested Ukraine might be behind the incidents and proposed a joint investigation. His remarks follow Moldovan accounts of drones entering its airspace; responsibility for the incidents remains disputed.

items.title: EU Commission proposes €45 billion for Ukraine in 2027
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed €45 billion in funding for Ukraine in 2027, saying it would cover roughly two-thirds of the country's projected needs. She expects partners to provide another €25 billion, with EU leaders scheduled to discuss the proposal at an emergency summit on November 26–27.

items.title: US House Republicans reportedly seek Ukraine aid cuts in defence bill
items.summary: Republican lawmakers are reportedly pushing to remove provisions on military assistance and intelligence sharing with Ukraine from the annual US defence authorization bill, alongside proposed sanctions on Russia. The changes are described as part of negotiations over congressional oversight, with the bill's final text expected in early December.

items.title: Sweden announces additional Ukraine military funding and Gripen support arrangements
items.summary: Sweden reportedly announced about $71 million in additional contributions to military-support funds for Ukraine, including air defence, long-range capabilities and US weapons procurement. A separate Swedish-British-Ukrainian arrangement concerns ammunition, equipment and spare parts for Gripen fighter aircraft.

items.title: EU reportedly hesitant to include Russian oil shipping ban in next sanctions package
items.summary: The European Commission may leave a proposed ban on maritime transport of Russian oil out of its 22nd sanctions package over concerns that member states would block it, according to a report attributed to Bloomberg. A similar proposal was reportedly removed during negotiations over the previous package.

items.title: German foreign minister rejects proposal for new European security architecture
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul rejected a Russian proposal for a new European security framework, arguing that existing agreed rules and principles should instead be respected. His response underscores continuing differences over the security arrangements surrounding negotiations on Ukraine.

items.title: Kyiv issues detailed bridge restrictions following November 17 strikes
items.summary: Kyiv authorities reportedly limited the South Bridge to lighter vehicles and public transport, while restricting the North Bridge to public transport and emergency vehicles. The Podilskyi Bridge faces temporary closures during air alerts, and the Paton Bridge is operating one-way on a timed schedule; two other crossings remain unrestricted.

items.title: Russian aircraft manufacturer delivers another batch of Su-34 bombers
items.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation announced another delivery of Su-34 fighter-bombers to the Defence Ministry after factory testing, describing it as the third publicly announced batch this year. The number of aircraft was not disclosed; the Su-34 is widely used to deploy glide bombs in the war.

items.title: Patriot missile production reportedly constrained by specialist French material
items.summary: The Pentagon reportedly faces a shortage of carbonised rayon used in the rocket motors of Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors, with the sole approved supplier, France's ArianeGroup, unable to rapidly expand deliveries. The reported bottleneck comes as Ukraine seeks more Patriot missiles from allied stockpiles; a new US production facility is not expected until 2030.

items.title: Geran drone reportedly strikes hangar housing An-124 at Hostomel airfield
items.summary: Footage reportedly shows a Russian Geran drone striking a hangar at Hostomel airfield near Kyiv where an An-124 Ruslan heavy transport aircraft was parked. The aircraft had reportedly remained in Ukraine since 2022 after maintenance left it unable to depart; the extent of any damage is unclear.

items.title: New images reportedly show damage at Motor Sich plant in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: Images circulated showing the reported aftermath of strikes on a building within the Motor Sich factory grounds in Zaporizhzhia on November 17. The account identified a location at the industrial complex but did not specify the building's function or the extent of damage.

items.title: Russian military says FPV drones destroyed two Ukrainian UAV control posts
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said FPV drone operators from its Southern Group of Forces destroyed two Ukrainian drone-control positions. The brief announcement did not identify the exact locations or provide further operational details.

items.title: Russian vessels reportedly begin clearing debris from damaged Crimean Bridge
items.summary: At least ten vessels, including tugs and a dredger, were reportedly operating around the damaged Crimean Bridge after the collapse of a road section into the Kerch-Yenikale Canal. Ship-tracking observations suggest smaller vessels may still be able to pass, while crews appear to be working to clear debris from the waterway.

items.title: Russia's FSB detains two men over alleged intelligence work for Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service says it arrested two residents of Khabarovsk Krai suspected of collecting information on industrial sites and military personnel for Ukrainian intelligence. The agency alleges one suspect obtained drone-control equipment and training for possible sabotage; a treason investigation has been opened.

items.title: Strikes reportedly hit energy and administrative sites in Odesa
items.summary: Explosions were reported in Odesa, with local accounts alleging that one strike hit an energy facility and another struck an administrative building. The report did not establish the extent of damage or any casualties.

items.title: Russian drone unit reports attacks on Ukrainian energy and logistics facilities
items.summary: A Russian unmanned-systems brigade reportedly carried out Geran-4 drone strikes against a logistics centre, a combined heat-and-power plant and a drone-storage facility. Footage was circulated purporting to show the attacks, but precise locations and damage assessments were not provided.

items.title: Russian diplomat warns of response to possible nuclear deployments in Eastern Europe
items.summary: A Russian delegation representative in Vienna warned that easing restrictions on nuclear-weapon deployments in Lithuania, Poland or other European countries would prompt countermeasures by Moscow's strategic deterrence forces. The remarks described a potential response rather than an announced deployment.

items.title: SAPO reports five suspects in alleged draft-evasion smuggling scheme
items.summary: SAPO and NABU say they notified five people of suspicion, including two serving Ukrainian border guards and a former official, over an alleged scheme to move draft-age men into Europe through Transnistria. Investigators say customers paid $5,000 each, including $1,500 allegedly passed to border guards; the agencies say an earlier investigation was closed before the case was reopened.

items.title: Russian airstrikes reportedly target Ukrainian positions in Sumy and Kharkiv
items.summary: Footage circulated of reported Russian airstrikes using four OFAB-250-270 bombs against a Ukrainian territorial-defence deployment site near Korenek in Sumy region and a FAB-3000 bomb against a crossing near Oskil in Kharkiv region. The extent of damage was not specified.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry describes ground-robot operations in Dnipropetrovsk sector
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said remotely operated ground vehicles from its 39th Guards Engineering Regiment are transporting supplies and clearing routes in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. The ministry said the vehicles can traverse rough terrain and assist with minefield clearance.

items.title: Ukrainian anti-corruption court sentences former forestry chief and wife
items.summary: NABU says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court sentenced a former head of the State Forest Resources Agency to 12 years in prison and his wife to 10 years in a bribery and money-laundering case. Both were tried in absentia, and the judgment can be appealed before it takes effect.

items.title: Russia says drone strike hit cargo ship bound for Odesa
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones struck a dry-cargo vessel at sea that it described as transporting military supplies to Odesa. The ministry did not identify the ship or provide a damage assessment.

items.title: Luhansk authorities report seven deaths in Ukrainian drone attacks
items.summary: Authorities in Russian-controlled Luhansk reportedly said seven people were killed in attacks on vehicles and civilians across several districts, including Starobilsk, Novoaidar and Troitske. The account also described injuries to several other residents.

items.title: Russian officials outline Putin-Trump meeting plans at APEC summit
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said no full-scale Putin-Trump negotiations were planned for November 19, while presidential aide Yuri Ushakov subsequently said a bilateral meeting would take place after the summit's plenary session. Officials also described a planned hour-long meeting involving Putin, Trump and Xi Jinping.

items.title: European Commission reportedly forecasts 20 million Russian drones in 2027
items.summary: The European Commission reportedly estimated that Russia could deploy 20 million drones in Ukraine during 2027, a figure understood to include small FPV systems. The reported projection is an estimate, not a confirmed production or deployment total.

items.title: Russian military analysis reports increased Ukrainian activity near Sumy
items.summary: A Russian battlefield assessment says Ukrainian small-unit activity has intensified along the Khoten-Mohrytsya line north of Sumy, with troops reportedly infiltrating forested areas rather than mounting a large offensive. It warns that a buildup could threaten Russian positions and potentially lead to operations toward the border.

items.title: Russia says artillery struck Ukrainian drone-control posts in Kharkiv region
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said a Giatsint-B artillery crew from its Sever Group shelled Ukrainian drone-control positions, equipment and personnel in Kharkiv region. The announcement did not specify the exact location or provide a damage assessment.

items.title: IAEA chief says agency cannot assign blame for attacks on Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
items.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said the agency cannot identify who is responsible for attacks on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant without independently verifiable evidence. Russia's Foreign Ministry has accused the agency of avoiding attributing responsibility to Ukraine.

items.title: Polish report alleges foiled false-flag operation near Kaliningrad
items.summary: Polish media reportedly alleged that intelligence services thwarted a plan to stage an incident near the Kaliningrad border using people posing as Ukrainian saboteurs, with the aim of blaming Ukraine and pressuring Poland over its support. The account offered no details of arrests or how the alleged operation was prevented.

items.title: Russia says air defences downed 51 Ukrainian drones over Krasnodar and Sea of Azov
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 51 Ukrainian drones during the day over Krasnodar Krai and the Sea of Azov. The announcement did not specify damage or casualties.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry reports drone strikes on vehicles in Sumy region
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said drone operators from its 56th Guards Air Assault Regiment struck Ukrainian vehicles and crews in Sumy region. The brief statement did not specify locations, losses or damage assessments.

items.title: EU diplomats reportedly question Kaja Kallas's role in Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: EU leaders reportedly left foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas off Europe's Ukraine negotiating team amid disagreements over her approach to Russia. Diplomats have criticized her independent initiatives, while Italy's Giorgia Meloni reportedly questioned her suitability for high-level negotiations.

items.title: Lviv retailer reportedly limits sunflower oil purchases after strikes
items.summary: A retailer in Lviv reportedly limited purchases of Ridnokrai sunflower oil to two bottles per transaction as shoppers stocked up following Russian strikes on Ukrainian oil-producing facilities. Ukraine's agriculture minister said a nationwide shortage was not expected.

items.title: Russia and China exploring joint weapons development and production
items.summary: Dmitry Shugaev, head of Russia's Federal Service for Military-Technical Cooperation, said Moscow and Beijing are exploring opportunities to jointly develop and manufacture weapons. No specific projects, agreements or timelines were announced in the reported remarks.

items.title: Russian strike assessment describes greater use of ballistic missiles in Ukraine
items.summary: A Russian military-focused assessment of recent strikes across Ukraine says ballistic missiles received greater emphasis, while jet-powered and propeller-driven drones were used in roughly equal numbers. It describes jet-powered drones as primarily targeting western and central Ukraine, without providing a detailed tally.

items.title: Italian opposition lawmakers call for closure of Ukraine's Myrotvorets website
items.summary: Members of Italy's opposition Five Star Movement in the European Parliament called for Ukraine's Myrotvorets website to be shut down, accusing it of spreading hatred and disinformation. Their statement represents a political demand, not an announced EU measure.

items.title: Evacuated Krasnoarmiisk resident alleges Ukrainian drone killed neighbours
items.summary: An elderly evacuee identified as Alexander told RT that a Ukrainian drone killed two of his neighbours in Krasnoarmiisk during autumn 2025. He also alleged that retreating Ukrainian troops displayed a dead Russian soldier at a checkpoint; these are the witness's allegations about earlier events.

items.title: Confrontation reported between residents and military recruiters in Odesa
items.summary: A confrontation reportedly broke out between local residents and Ukrainian military recruitment officers in Odesa. The account says residents forced the officers to retreat, but provides no details about injuries, arrests or the circumstances leading to the dispute.

items.title: Russian Rubikon drone unit releases November 18 combat activity roundup
items.summary: A Russian military drone unit released a video roundup describing operations in Donbas, the Sloviansk and Sumy sectors, including strikes coordinated with aircraft, remote mining of Ukrainian supply routes and FPV drone interceptions. The accompanying account says the compilation contains 277 episodes, without establishing independent damage totals.

items.title: Crimean Bridge rail traffic suspended after reported Ukrainian attack
items.summary: Crimean leader Sergey Aksyonov said Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge for a third time this week, prompting authorities to suspend rail traffic while assessing damage. The extent of damage and the duration of the suspension were not specified.

items.title: Pentagon official reportedly leaves meeting before Ukrainian defence briefing
items.summary: The Telegraph reportedly said US Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby left a meeting with European allies before Ukrainian Defence Minister Khmara could deliver a classified battlefield briefing. The account says Colby had criticized Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russian territory.

items.title: Finnish ICEYE unveils higher-resolution Gen5 radar satellite platform
items.summary: ICEYE's new Gen5 synthetic-aperture radar platform reportedly offers imagery resolution as fine as 11 centimetres and improved imaging capacity, including in darkness and cloud cover. A Russian military analysis says ICEYE imagery is already used to support Ukrainian reconnaissance and strike assessments, making the upgrade relevant to battlefield intelligence.

items.title: Ukrainian monitors warn of possible missile strikes on Kyiv infrastructure
items.summary: Ukrainian monitoring channels reportedly issued a 48-hour ballistic-missile threat alert, naming several Kyiv bridges, thermal power plants and the Nyvky substation as potential targets. The warning describes a possible attack, not strikes that have occurred.

items.title: Musk says Ukraine's front depends on Starlink connectivity
items.summary: Elon Musk said Ukraine's military front would collapse immediately without Starlink, underscoring the satellite network's role in Ukrainian military communications. His statement is an assessment, not a reported change to Starlink service.
